_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.english_concept: fancy/cool text (generic umbrella term)
phrases.content_surface: title, meta, hero, FAQ, homepage prose
phrases.usage_guidance: The site's own established primary umbrella term for the whole Unicode-styled-text concept on the NO homepage (title, meta description, hero copy, and 4+ FAQ answers). Use as the default generic term when referring to the overall generator/output, not to one specific family.
phrases.good_example: Bruk kul tekst i visningsnavn, bio og status.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use for one narrow style family (e.g. bold specifically) — it's the umbrella term.

phrases.english_concept: stylish/decorative (adjective for text, names, letters)
phrases.content_surface: title, hero, FAQ, guide prose, library CTA sections
phrases.usage_guidance: Used site-wide as the supporting adjective for styled output: 'stilig navn' (guide/trygt-discord-navn title), 'stilig tekst' (library CTA headings), 'stilige bokstaver'. Independently confirmed as natural forum usage on diskusjon.no ('stilig navn på klan?' thread title). Safe as a secondary descriptor alongside 'kul tekst'.
phrases.good_example: Slik lager du et stilig Discord-navn uten å bli filtrert

phrases.english_concept: fancy (borrowed English adjective, casual register)
phrases.usage_guidance: Used untranslated as a casual loanword directly before a Norwegian noun with no 'kopier' modifier attached: 'Lim en fancy skrift der' (paste a fancy font there), 'et fancy navn'. Confirms fancy+noun is a natural bare construction in NO prose, not just an SEO artifact. Keep to casual/Discord-adjacent copy; do not use in formal/legal copy.
phrases.good_example: Blir jeg bannlyst på Discord for å ha et fancy navn?
phrases.avoid_when: Formal, legal, or accessibility-explainer copy — use 'stilig' or 'kul' there instead.

phrases.english_concept: italic (slanted) typeface style — the TRUE dictionary meaning of 'kursiv' in Norwegian
phrases.usage_guidance: Standard Norwegian dictionary/editorial term. Confirmed directly: korrekturavdelingen.no opens with 'Kursiv er skråstilt tekst' (kursiv is slanted text) and defines it purely as the italic typeface tradition (chancery-hand-derived slanted type), with no mention of cursive/joined handwriting. Reserve 'kursiv' for the ITALIC font family/style only.
phrases.good_example: Kursiv er skråstilt tekst.
phrases.avoid_when: Never use 'kursiv' to label a flowing/joined cursive-script Unicode style (𝓬𝓾𝓻𝓼𝓲𝓿𝓮) — that is a different concept in Norwegian. See NO-005.

phrases.english_concept: special characters
phrases.usage_guidance: Standard, natural NO compound noun for special characters/symbols used to decorate names. Matches prior existing-dictionary evidence (diskusjon.no 'symboler til navn' threads).
phrases.good_example: Gratis generator for kursiv tekst — spesialtegn til bio, navn og signaturer.

phrases.english_concept: symbols (collection/library sense)
phrases.usage_guidance: The dominant, heavily-used term across every no/library/* page (69, 48, 45, 44... occurrences per page) — this is the correct primary term for the library/symbol collection pillar and should stay the anchor term; do not replace with 'tegn' (too generic/technical) or 'ikoner' (wrong register — implies app icons, not Unicode glyphs).
phrases.good_example: Symboler til å kopiere og lime inn — hjerte, stjerne, pil og mer

phrases.english_concept: copy and paste (action)
phrases.content_surface: page titles (suffix convention), CTA buttons, FAQ how-to steps
phrases.usage_guidance: Grammatically correct and universally understood as the action itself — safe and necessary in how-to steps, button labels ('Kopier'), and toast confirmations ('Kopiert!'). Use freely as a UI action label. See NO-009 for the distinct, narrower finding about how this phrase behaves as a SEARCH-QUERY modifier (largely it doesn't) — that is a query-formulation nuance, not a reason to avoid the action phrase in UI/CTA copy.
phrases.good_example: Skriv eller lim inn teksten din i feltet øverst, og trykk deretter Kopier på stilen du liker.
phrases.avoid_when: As a title-suffix on every single page indiscriminately without checking whether it duplicates the anchor keyword of a sibling page already ranking for the bare noun.

phrases.english_concept: gaming/in-game display name
phrases.usage_guidance: Both forms coexist naturally in the wild: 'spillenavn' (native compound) and borrowed 'gaming navn' are used interchangeably by the same forum users in the same thread. No strong preference found; either is natural.
phrases.good_example: lurer pa om noen av dere har noen tips om et spille navn til meg?

phrases.english_concept: cool (name/style quality)
phrases.usage_guidance: Natural casual descriptor when a forum user asks for name ideas. Safe for informal generator-example copy, gaming pages; avoid in formal/accessibility explainer sections.
phrases.good_example: noen 'kult' eller spessielt (gaming-name request thread)

phrases.english_concept: unique / not common (desired quality of a name/style, distinct from generic 'unique')
phrases.usage_guidance: The way Norwegian gamers actually phrase the 'unique/not common' idea is negatively framed — 'not what hundreds of others already have' — rather than a single adjective. Good raw material for FAQ/prose on a gaming-name generator page: address the 'will this look like everyone else's' worry directly rather than just claiming 'unique'.
phrases.good_example: Finn noe orginalt, noe ikke flere hundre andre har allerede.

phrases.english_concept: clan name / clan tag
phrases.usage_guidance: Recurring, sustained forum topic across many years (threads from 2007 through 2020s) — 'klan navn' is the standard term; tags are conventionally wrapped in brackets or asterisks before/around the name, e.g. '[KIMS]', '{NV}', '*KIMS*'. Relevant if a clan/tag-generator feature is ever scoped for NO.
phrases.good_example: stilig navn på klan?

phrases.english_concept: decoration / ornamentation on a styled name (neutral term, plus its 'excessive' form)
phrases.usage_guidance: This is the site's own well-established, natural native term for 'decoration' — used repeatedly and consistently across the Discord safe-naming guide ('tung pynt', 'pyntestrenger', 'et navn er ikke risikabelt fordi det er pyntet'). This is the tasteful, non-pejorative way to talk about excessive styling on-page (contrast with the pejorative slang 'fjortis', NO-013, which should stay off-page).
phrases.good_example: Et stilig navn er ikke risikabelt fordi det er pyntet. Det blir risikabelt når pynten hindrer deg i å bli funnet, lest eller skilt fra andre.

phrases.english_concept: confusable/look-alike characters (used to impersonate another user)
phrases.usage_guidance: Natural, clear NO compound for the technical concept of homoglyph/confusable characters, used repeatedly and consistently in the Discord safe-naming guide's identity-theft and searchability sections. Good, precise term — no better alternative found.
phrases.good_example: å bruke forvekslingstegn for å etterligne en annen ekte bruker, en moderator eller et verifisert merke

phrases.english_concept: identity theft (in the context of impersonating another Discord user via lookalike characters)
phrases.usage_guidance: Standard dictionary NO term, correctly and naturally applied to the narrower Discord-impersonation context (not just financial/legal identity theft). Appropriate as used.
phrases.good_example: filteret mot identitetstyveri

phrases.english_concept: display name vs. username vs. nickname — the three-way platform-identity distinction
phrases.usage_guidance: The site correctly keeps these three distinct and uses each in the right place: 'brukernavn' for the strict a-z0-9 @-handle, 'visningsnavn' for the freely-styled display layer, 'kallenavn' for Discord server-level nicknames. This distinction is load-bearing for the site's own Discord-formatting guides (styled text works in visningsnavn/kallenavn, not brukernavn) — keep it precise, don't collapse the three into one word.
phrases.good_example: Lim en fancy skrift der [i @brukernavnet], og Discord nekter å lagre den. Style visningsnavnet i stedet.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'brukernavn' loosely to mean 'display name' — the site's own accuracy about platform character limits depends on keeping these separate.

phrases.english_concept: smiley/emoji face
phrases.content_surface: library page title, hero, JSON-LD alternateName
phrases.usage_guidance: The genuinely native Norwegian word for a face emoji/emoticon, distinct from the borrowed 'emoji' — used consistently and correctly as the page's anchor term (title, H1, alternateName variants: 'Smilefjes betydning', 'Glade fjes emoji', 'Smilefjes kopier og lim inn'). Good model of a fully native (non-borrowed) term winning over the English loanword where one exists.
phrases.good_example: Smilefjes — betydning og når du bør bruke dem

phrases.english_concept: aesthetic (style descriptor, borrowed English adjective)
phrases.content_surface: homepage prose (family list, FAQ), library symbol prose
phrases.usage_guidance: Used untranslated as a style-family label ('aesthetic' listed alongside 'fet skrift', 'kursiv', 'håndskrift' as one of the ~12 style families) and as a loose adjective ('sjeldne aesthetic-hjerter'). This matches how the term is actually used by Norwegian-speaking internet/social-media culture — there is no natural NO equivalent found ('estetisk' is the dictionary translation but reads clinical/art-critical, not the internet-culture sense). Keep scoped to informal generator-example/library copy per this site's borrowed-term register rule; do not promote into formal explainer prose.
phrases.good_example: sjeldne aesthetic-hjerter som ᥫ᭡ og ღ
phrases.avoid_when: Formal/accessibility explainer paragraphs — use 'stilig' or 'dekorativ' there instead.

phrases.english_concept: pet name / term of endearment for a romantic partner
phrases.content_surface: romantic/relationship-naming feature copy (does not currently exist on no/)
phrases.usage_guidance: The correct, distinct NO term for a romantic pet name (not the same as 'kallenavn', which is a generic nickname). Confirmed via VG (major Norwegian newspaper) editorial coverage citing real examples: 'pus', 'skatt', 'trusepus'. Relevant if any romantic/relationship-address naming content is ever built for NO — do not substitute the generic 'kallenavn'.
phrases.good_example: Kjælenavn på kjæresten styrker forholdet (VG headline)
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'kallenavn' as a substitute when the context is specifically romantic.

phrases.english_concept: zalgo/glitch text (borrowed community term)
phrases.usage_guidance: 'Zalgo' has no Norwegian equivalent and is correctly kept as the borrowed proper-noun-style term, glued to the native suffix '-tekst'. This is the only sensible approach — do not attempt a NO translation of 'zalgo'.
phrases.good_example: Er zalgo-tekst mot Discord-reglene?

phrases.english_concept: text rendering as boxes/squares/question marks (missing glyph / 'tofu' problem)
phrases.usage_guidance: The site's homepage FAQ already covers this concept ('Ruter, tomme blokker eller spørsmålstegn') without using the exact phrase 'firkanter' — real Norwegian users describe the same failure as text turning into 'rare tegn' (weird characters) or, per Dagbladet mainstream coverage of the emoji version of this problem, 'en firkant med spørsmålstegn i' (a square with a question mark in it). Both are natural, safe troubleshooting phrasings.
phrases.good_example: Får du bare opp en firkant med spørsmålstegn i? (Dagbladet)

phrases.english_concept: bio (Instagram/social profile bio, borrowed English noun)
phrases.usage_guidance: Used untranslated and compounded freely with Norwegian ('Instagram-bio', 'bioen', 'i bio, navn og bildetekst') — this is simply how Norwegian social-media users refer to a profile bio; there is no separate native word in active use for this specific sense. Safe, natural, no substitution needed.
phrases.good_example: Gjør bioen eller visningsnavnet mer personlig med håndskrift, fet skrift, fine bokstaver...

phrases.english_concept: idiom for confused/frustrated head-scratching over a tech problem
phrases.content_surface: authentic voice/idiom for describing user frustration with input methods

phrases.native_phrase: navn i runer / navnet i runer
phrases.english_concept: name in runes -- the natural NO compound for transliterating a name into runic script
phrases.content_surface: vocabulary anchor if this heritage-adjacent niche is ever evaluated further

phrases.english_concept: Younger Futhark rune-system sub-variant names (long-branch / short-twig runes)
phrases.content_surface: precise native terminology for Younger Futhark sub-variants, in case accuracy is needed for any rune-adjacent content

phrases.english_concept: cool/decorative letters — the vernacular anchor phrase for the fancy-font job
phrases.usage_guidance: Strong candidate for the NO homepage/hero title — found independently, 3 years apart, in two unrelated communities (gaming forum 2006, wedding-planning forum 2009), which is a better real-language signal than a single-source hit.
